products.name: Pair of armchairs model 3758 A designed by Kaare Klint for Rud. Rasmussen
products.description: Model designed in 1927 for the Danish Museum of Decorative Art, produced by Rud Rasmussen in the 1940's. Kaare Klint was the father of Scandinavian modernism and is responsible for bringing Danish design to the centre stage.

products.name: Pair of stools
products.description: Beech wood frames raised on four tapered legs. Gently curved, saddle-shaped seats offering good comfort.

products.name: A set of six armchairs 'Model 350' designed by Peter Hvidt and Orla Mølgaard-Nielsen for Søborg Møbler
products.description: These 'Model 350' armchairs were designed by Peter Hvidt and Orla Mølgaard-Nielsen for Søborg Møbelfabrik and presented publicly at the Cabinetmakers’ Guild Exhibition in 1958. The chairs are constructed in teak, with a clearly articulated, architectural frame defined by straight lines, sharp angles and precise joinery.

products.name: Set of ten dining chairs designed by Aino Aalto for Artek
products.description: A set of ten dining chairs designed by Aino Aalto for Artek, executed in mahogany with upholstered seats and backs in patinated Niger leather.

products.name: Addition sofa model KK 8201
products.description: Two-seat addition sofa with button-tufted leather upholstery on a solid mahogany frame, in the manner of 1940s Swedish cabinetmaker furniture.

products.name: Armchair 42 'Small Paimio' designed by Alvar Aalto
products.description: Armchair 42 – or “Small Paimio” – was designed by Alvar Aalto for the Paimio Sanatorium in 1931. The frame is made from laminated birch shaped to produce a cantilevered chair; the seat and back are created from one piece of form-pressed plywood.

products.name: A pair of armchairs and sofa for Paul Boman
products.material: Brazilian rosewood and savak wool upholstery
products.description: Sofa and armchair set with sculptural rosewood frames and ivory savak wool upholstery, made for cabinetmaker Paul Boman.

products.name: Chieftain armchair
products.description: Chieftain armchair designed by Arne Norell, with a wide saddle-leather seat and back resting on a sculptural teak frame.

products.name: Armchair designed by Frits Henningsen
products.material: Stained wooden legs, seat and back upholstered in wool
products.description: This armchair is the work of Danish designer and cabinetmaker Frits Henningsen, who was active in the first half of the 20th century and is known for producing his furniture entirely within his own Copenhagen workshop. Rather than relying on external manufacturers, he oversaw each stage of construction himself, from joinery to final finishing.

products.name: Armchair designed by Hans Frost Nielsen
products.description: This armchair was designed in 1974 by the Danish craftsman Hans Frost Nielsen. This armchair is a rare example of a full-scale furniture design produced under his own name.

products.name: An Art Nouveau armchair
products.description: Gustavian style armchair with a pale grey-green lacquered frame, gilded detailing and white upholstered seat and back.

products.name: Bench designed by Hans Wegner for Johannes Hansen
products.description: Reflecting Wegner’s characteristic design philosophy, this bench is a masterpiece of simplicity, functionality, and timeless beauty. The sturdy, tapered legs provide a strong foundation while maintaining a light visual presence.

products.name: Chaise lounge designed by Bruno Mathsson
products.material: Beech, saddle strap of black natural flax, neck pillow of grey wool
products.description: This reclining chaise lounge, model 36 by Bruno Mathsson, is a quintessential example of Swedish modernism and Scandinavian design. Designed with Mathsson’s characteristic focus on ergonomics, the beech frame is elegantly bent into a continuous, flowing line that follows the natural contours of the body.

products.name: Chaise longue for Louis G Thiersen
products.description: This chaise longue reflects a restrained neoclassical influence within early 20th-century Danish furniture design. The elongated form is defined by a single scrolled backrest and a continuous upholstered seat, allowing for a reclining position while maintaining a compact footprint.

products.name: Children’s chair 'Lilla M' designed by Caroline Schlyter
products.description: Lacquered plywood construction formed from a single continuous curve. Sculptural, flowing profile integrating seat, backrest and base, with a circular cut-out detail to the back.

products.name: 'Clam' Chair designed by Arnold Madsen for Madsen & Schubell
products.description: The ‘Clam’, upholstered in soft sheepskin, is among the most comfortable chairs imaginable – it is both a recognisable and desirable Scandinavian design. As the name indicates, the design resembles the sea creature with a shell in two parts.

products.name: Corner sofa 'Athén'
products.description: Corner sofa with a woven rattan frame and cream upholstered cushions, in the manner of 1940s Swedish modernism.

products.name: Daybed designed by Erik Riisager Hansen for Haslev, Denmark.
products.description: This daybed, designed by Erik Riisager and produced by Haslev in the 1950s, reflects the restrained and functional approach characteristic of Danish furniture from the period. The piece is defined by its elongated, slightly tapered form and subtly raised ends, which provide both visual balance and practical support.

products.name: Daybed designed by Erik Riisager Hansen for Haslev, Denmark.
products.description: This daybed, designed by Erik Riisager and produced by Haslev in the 1950s, reflects the restrained and functional approach characteristic of Danish furniture from the period. The piece is defined by its elongated, slightly tapered form and subtly raised ends, which provide both visual balance and practical support.

products.name: Daybed designed by Ib Kofod-Larsen
products.description: The daybed reflects Ib Kofod-Larsen’s approach to functional furniture developed during the post-war period in Denmark. The design combines a solid walnut frame with a cane sleeping surface, allowing the piece to function both as seating and as a bed.

products.name: Easy chair designed by Otto Schulz for Boet, Sweden, 1940s
products.description: This vintage armchair is a refined example of Otto Schulz’s distinctive contribution to Swedish design. Inspired by the classical Greek klismos chair as well as his own well-known “Sulla” model, Schulz developed a broad, sculptural seat with a softly curved backrest that embraces the sitter.

products.name: Easy chair 'Star', designed by Mats Theselius for Källemo,
products.material: Leather, tubular frame and mouldings of chromed metal
products.description: “Star” is an armchair conceived by Swedish designer Mats Theselius in collaboration with the manufacturer Källemo. Executed circa 2009, this limited‑edition piece (of a run of 360) blends sculptural presence with refined materiality.

products.name: The Flag Halyard chair
products.material: Original green lacquered steel frame with beech shoes, halyard line and sheepskin
products.description: Flag Halyard chair designed by Hans J. Wegner, with a halyard-line seat, green lacquered steel frame and long-haired sheepskin throw.

products.name: Easy chair Designed by Otto Schulz for Boet
products.description: This vintage furniture armchair is an elegant example of Otto Schulz’s sophisticated Swedish design language. Drawing on the classical Greek klismos and his own “Sulla” model, Schulz developed a generous, sculptural seat with a sweeping back that curves gently around the sitter.

products.name: Easy chairs designed by Bodil Kjaer for Harbo Sølvsten
products.description: "The chairs were designed for the modernist house "Doktorn 5" in the town Laholm, Sweden, in 1956, by architect Svend Bøgh-Andersen (1916-1984), who built and decorated it for him and his wife Hanne (1920-2015)" Four available. Sold individually.

products.name: Folding stool 'Guldhøj’ designed by Poul Hundevad
products.description: This stool’s design was inspired by a fascinating piece of Danish history. In 1891, a team of archaeologists led by Vilhelm Boye excavated the Guldhøj burial mound in southern Jutland; a burial site dating back to around 1400 BCE.

products.name: Sofa designed by N.D. Hansen and Flemming Johansen for cabinetmaker Ove Lander
products.description: This very rare three-seater sofa was first exhibited at the 1936 Copenhagen Cabinetmakers’ Guild Exhibition, an annual furniture exhibition and competition held from 1927 to 1966. The sofa was made by the master cabinetmaker Ole Lander and was produced in very small numbers, if at all.

products.name: Lounge chair 'Pernilla 3' designed by Bruno Mathsson for Karl Mathsson
products.description: The lounge chair ‘Pernilla 3’ was designed in 1944 by Bruno Mathsson. The model was named after the journalist Pernilla Thunberger who visited Bruno Mathsson for an interview earlier that same year.

products.name: Oxford dining set model AJ 711
products.description: Dining set comprising a round pedestal table and four high-backed Oxford chairs, all in polished rosewood.

products.name: Pair of 'Basket Club' armchairs
products.description: Pair of basket armchairs with round handwoven cane seats set within sculpted rosewood frames.

products.name: Pair of armchairs ‘Eva’ designed by Bruno Mathsson for Karl Mathsson
products.description: With its characteristically curved legs and armrests, this iconic chair model "Eva" exemplifies Swedish functionalism. The comfortable seat is composed of beautifully patinated plaited leather straps in cognac — "Eva" in leather was only introduced in the 1960s.

products.name: Pair of easy chairs
products.description: Pair of high-backed easy chairs in mahogany with buttoned upholstery in patinated Niger leather.

products.name: A set of four chair model 'Corall' designed by Axel Einar Hjorth for Nordiska Kompaniet, Sweden
products.material: Ebonised birch, woven cane, upholstered cushion
products.description: This set of four ‘Corall’ chairs, designed by Axel Einar Hjorth for Nordiska Kompaniet in 1937, reflects the practicality and simplicity characteristic of Swedish design during this period. Created for summer houses and cabins, the Corall series was designed to suit homes often located in natural or coastal environments.

products.name: Pair of easy chairs designed by Frits Schlegel
products.description: This pair of easy chairs was designed by Frits Schlegel in Denmark in the 1950s. The chairs are constructed in solid ash with backs and seats in woven rattan cane.

products.name: Pair of armchairs
products.description: Pair of 'Elizabeth' armchairs with high winged backs in patinated black leather on rosewood frames, designed by Ib Kofod-Larsen.

products.name: Pair of chairs designed by Erik Chambert
products.description: Pair of side chairs in birch with woven cane backs and rust-coloured upholstered seats.

products.name: Armchair
products.material: Oak legs upholstered with original natural leather
products.description: Wingback armchair with sculpted oak legs and original natural leather upholstery in warm cognac.

products.name: Rocking chair model RA 4032
products.material: Chromed tubular steel and vinyl covered springs
products.description: Rocking chaise with a bent chromed tubular steel frame and a vinyl-covered spring seat.

products.name: Set of six dining chairs 'Model 465' designed by Helge Sibast & Børge Rammeskov for Sibast Møbler
products.description: These 'Model 465' dining chairs by Helge Sibast and Børge Rammeskov for Sibast Møbler represent a refined expression of Danish modern design. Crafted in rosewood, the frames display a rich, expressive grain that enhances the sculptural quality of the design, while the upholstered seats in blue wool introduce a soft contrast in both colour and texture.

products.name: Set of ten butterfly dining chairs
products.description: Set of ten dining chairs with sculpted butterfly-shaped backs in white above teak frames.

products.name: Snake chair model PH 8849
products.description: Snake chair with a coiled chromed steel base and tartan plaid seat and back.

products.name: Sofa 'Elizabeth'
products.material: Frame in rosewood, seat and back upholstered in black leather
products.description: Two-seat sofa with a curved rosewood frame and black leather seat and back, designed by Ib Kofod-Larsen.

products.name: Sofa designed by Axel Einar Hjorth for Nordiska Kompaniet
products.description: This corner sofa designed by Axel Einar Hjorth in the 1930s for Nordiska Kompaniet reflects the refined elegance of Swedish furniture from the transitional period between Swedish Grace and early functionalism. Upholstered in velvet, the sofa is composed of two gently angled sections that form a welcoming corner arrangement.

products.name: Sofa ‘Royal’ designed by Werner West for Oy Stockmann AB
products.description: The “Royal” sofa by Werner West is wonderfully comfortable and elegant with its high, enveloping backrest and integrated arms. The cut-out fronts and fine Boucle upholstery give the sizeable piece its modern aesthetic, while the tall back legs offer strong support by kicking out for extra balance.

products.name: Sofa model FH 8948
products.material: Mahogany and pearl spiked upholstery in red leather
products.description: Three-seat sofa with pearl-spiked red leather upholstery and curved mahogany armrests.

products.name: Tabouret model SL 14
products.description: Gustavian style tabouret with a grey-green lacquered frame, gilded ornamental details and white upholstered seat.

products.name: Coffee table designed by Frode Holm for Illums Bolighus
products.description: Coffee table with a red lacquered steel frame and top decorated with black and white enamel squares.

products.name: Desk designed by Alvar Andersson for Hyresgästföreningen, retailed by G.A. Berg
products.material: Black lacquered birch, elm and pewter inlay
products.description: Gustaf Axel Berg ran his own shop and workshop on Kungsgatan in central Stockholm between 1933 and 1944. His production was mostly on commission for offices in the 1930s and, as functionalism slowly gained recognition, also for private interiors in the late 1930s and 1940s.

products.name: Desk designed by a Danish Cabinetmaker
products.description: This Danish cabinetmaker’s desk was made in the 1930s from root wood and nutwood. The front is arranged with five drawers, set within a rectilinear frame and raised on straight legs.

products.name: Desk model JH571 designed by Hans J. Wegner for Johannes Hansen
products.description: The Architect’s Desk, model JH571, was designed by Hans J. Wegner for the Copenhagen cabinetmaker Johannes Hansen in 1953 and first presented in 1954 at the Copenhagen Cabinetmakers’ Guild Exhibition.

products.name: Desk, designed by Helge Sibast for Sibast Furniture
products.description: This executive desk, designed by Helge Sibast exemplifies Danish modern design with its clean lines, refined craftsmanship, and functional elegance. Featuring ample storage, refined brass details, and clean architectural lines, it serves as both a practical workspace and a statement piece.

products.name: Desk designed by Tove Kindt-Larsen and Edvard Kindt-Larsen for Thorald Madsen. H.
products.description: This freestanding desk by Tove and Edvard Kindt-Larsen is distinguished by the subtle shaping of the tabletop, where the edges rise slightly to form a shallow surround. Produced by cabinetmaker Thorald Madsen, the piece reflects a careful balance between utility and proportion typical of their work from the mid 20th century.

products.name: Dining table model O.K.
products.material: Vavona burl top, base in stained birch
products.description: Extendable dining table with an oval vavona burl top on a stained birch pedestal base with curved legs.

products.name: Dining table
products.description: This Swedish Modern dining table from the 1930s/40s embodies the elegant simplicity and craftsmanship characteristic of the period. Constructed with a sturdy oak frame, the table features gently tapering legs that lend a refined, sculptural quality.

products.name: Dining table designed by Arne Vodder for Sibast
products.description: This rosewood dining table features a seamlessly integrated extendable design, allowing for effortless expansion to accommodate larger gatherings without compromising its elegant profile. Precision joinery and expert craftsmanship are evident in the table’s solid frame and smooth extension mechanism, ensuring stability and ease of use.

products.name: Dining table designed by Hans J. Wegner for Andreas Tuck
products.description: Drop-leaf dining table with crossed sabre legs in teak and oak, accented with brass fittings.

products.name: Dining table 'Pyramid' designed by Carl Malmsten for J.O Carlsson
products.description: The Pyramid dining table was designed by Carl Malmsten in the early 1940s and produced in Sweden by J.O. Carlsson.

products.name: Occasional table
products.description: Rosewood game table with a reversible chessboard top, fitted drawers and original casters.

products.name: Magazine table designed by Bruno Mathsson  for Firma Karl Mathsson
products.material: Top in masur birch, legs of layer glued birch
products.description: This magazine table by Bruno Mathsson, produced by Firma Karl Mathsson in Värnamo and designed in 1964, is notable for combining a low table with integrated magazine storage in a single structure. The table belongs to a period in Mathsson’s career when he focused on lightweight wooden constructions and furniture intended for everyday use.

products.name: Occasional table / Bench model 5274, designed by Börge Mogensen for Fredericia Stolefabrik
products.description: This iconic design by Børge Mogensen, model 5274, was created for Fredericia Stolefabrik and remains a defining example of mid-century Danish modernism. The versatile piece is crafted with a solid oak frame and features a woven rattan top, often referred to as star weave or star rattan, which adds a distinctive texture to the piece.

products.name: Occasional table model 2168 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Josef Frank’s occasional table model 2168 is one of his rarer models. Its beautifully carved, turned legs give it a lighter and more playful aesthetic.

products.name: Occasional table 'Model AT-10' designed by Hans J Wegner for Andreas Tuck
products.description: The AT-10 occasional table, designed by Hans J. Wegner for Andreas Tuck in the 1950s, exemplifies Wegner's ability to combine functionality with simple, elegant design.

products.name: Occasional table designed by Frits Schlegel
products.description: The intriguing combination of rosewood and patinated brass is emphasised by the shape of this large occasional table from 1949. The offset slats that make up the round shelf under the table’s surface create a diagonal pattern, which lightens the overall design.

products.name: Side table model 6 designed by Helge Vestergaard Jensen manufactured by Jason Møbler
products.description: Side table 'Model 6' in rosewood produced by Jason Møbler demonstrates Helge Vestergaard Jensen’s disciplined approach to proportion and material. Although Jensen’s output was relatively limited, this makes his pieces today highly collectible, valued for their refined detailing and material integrity.

products.name: Occasional table designed by Mogens Lassen for T. Madsen
products.description: This occasional table was designed by Mogens Lassen for the Danish cabinetmaker T. Madsen in 1953.

products.name: Occasional table PK61 designed by Poul Kjaerholm for E. Kold Christensen
products.material: Steel and Porsgrunn marble with fossils
products.description: The PK61 table, designed by Poul Kjærholm in 1956, is a clear expression of the designer’s philosophy of structural clarity and material honesty. The table consists of four identical brushed steel elements that support a square marble top, forming a composition in which every part of the construction is visible.

products.name: Occasional table designed by Thomas Sandell, for Asplund
products.description: The significance of this piece lies in its contrasts. Initially designed for the company Asplund, the table has a solid birch top with a built-in fruit bowl on a green lacquered base.

products.name: Occasional table
products.material: Mahogany foldable frame and top with raised edge, brass fittings
products.description: Brazillian rosewood.

products.name: Occasional table 'Tulip' designed by Eero Saarinen for Knoll International
products.description: The Tulip table, designed by Eero Saarinen in the mid-1950s for Knoll, is one of the most recognisable pieces of twentieth-century modern furniture. The design pairs a circular Carrara marble top with a single pedestal base, creating a clear and elegant silhouette.

products.name: Pair of bedside tables 'Model 914' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Model 914 is a refined bedside table designed by Josef Frank in the 1950s for Svenskt Tenn. Executed in mahogany, the design is defined by its clear proportions: a rectangular top with raised edges, a single drawer fitted with a curved brass handle, and an open shelf below for additional storage.

products.name: Pair of bedside tables for DUX
products.description: The colonial-style combination of cane, rattan, and teak makes this Scandinavian bedside table design particularly interesting. The woven edges and metal handles create a striking decorative contrast.

products.name: 'Schroeder' occasional table designed by Gerrit Rietveld
products.material: Red, white, black, yellow and blue lacquered wood
products.description: The ‘Schroeder’ side table is an excellent example of the bold geometry and visionary design of the De Stijl movement. Produced by G.A. van de Groenekan, the table features an eye-catching composition of primary colours paired with clean, angular lines.

products.name: Serving trolley model 756 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: This serving trolley, model 756, was designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn during the 1940s. Executed in veneered walnut with brass details, the piece is characterised by its balanced proportions and light construction.

products.name: Set of four nesting tables designed by Aksel Kjersgaard
products.description: This set of four nesting tables, designed by Aksel Kjersgaard in Denmark during the 1960s, exemplifies the refined simplicity of Danish Modern design. Crafted from Brazilian rosewood, the tables feature clean lines and a minimalist rectangular form.

products.name: Sewing table designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: This sewing table was designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn in Sweden during the mid-twentieth century. Veneered in walnut and fitted with brass details, it combines practical storage with the light, domestic character that defines much of Frank’s furniture.

products.name: Side table designed by Anti Hakkarainen for Taidetakomo Hakkarainen
products.description: This side table, designed by Anti Hakkarainen in 1949 and produced by his workshop Taidetakomo Hakkarainen, combines expressive ironwork with a richly detailed mosaic surface. The wrought iron base is composed of slender legs shaped into rope-like twists, a technique closely associated with Hakkarainen’s metalwork.

products.name: Side table designed by Carl Axel Acking for Svenska Möbelfabrikerna Bodafors
products.description: Side table with a slatted teak top and softly bent legs, designed by Carl Axel Acking for Bodafors.

products.name: Side table designed by Jens Quistgaard
products.description: Executed in teak, the table features a circular top with a gently recessed centre, functioning as a removable tray. The top is constructed from multiple segments, carefully joined to emphasise the natural variation of the wood grain.

products.name: Side table designed by Sten Blomberg for David Blomberg AB
products.material: Black painted and nickel plated top and fittings
products.description: This side table was designed by Sten Blomberg for David Blomberg AB in Sweden in 1933. Executed in black-painted birch with a nickel-plated top and fittings, it reflects the shift in Swedish furniture design during the early 1930s, when the refinement of Swedish Grace began to give way to the more rational language of functionalism.

products.name: Sideboard designed by Axel Einar Hjorth
products.description: Sideboard in solid oak with two drawers fitted with leather-covered handles and brass details, designed by Axel Einar Hjorth.

products.name: Table in the style of Josef Frank
products.material: Mahogany base and walnut root top
products.description: Free-form side table with a figured walnut root top on a mahogany base, made in the style of Josef Frank.

products.name: Table designed by Alvar Aalto for Artek
products.description: This table, designed by Alvar Aalto for Artek in the 1970s, reflects Aalto’s hallmark design principles of simplicity and functionality. Constructed from lacquered birch with a durable laminate top, the table embodies the clean lines and natural materials central to Aalto’s modernist philosophy.

products.name: Table model 70 designed by Alvar Aalto for G. A. Berg
products.description: The Table, model 70, designed by Alvar Aalto for G. A.

products.name: Table with a pair of benches
products.description: Solid pine table with a live-edge top and a pair of matching benches, supported on organically shaped root bases.

products.name: Tray table designed by Rut Bryk for Arabia
products.material: Rectangular top in polychrome painted faience
products.description: Between 1944 and 1947, Rut Bryk created a limited series of trays for Arabia, featuring motifs that ranged from still lifes to depictions of life events such as funerals and, as in this case, weddings. Interestingly, Rut Bryk married Tapio Wirkkala in 1945 — just one year before the tray in question was made.

products.name: Trolley model 901 designed by Alvar Aalto
products.material: Frame in birch, panels in black linoleum
products.description: Alvar Aalto designed the Tea Trolley 901 in 1936, during a highly productive period that included his architectural work for the Finnish Pavilion at the 1937 Paris World’s Fair. The trolley reflects his broader interest in creating a complete visual and spatial language for interiors — furniture that complemented his architecture both functionally and emotionally.

products.name: Wall hung table designed by Helge Vestergaard Jensen, for Peder Pedersen
products.description: Wall-hung drop-leaf table in brazilian rosewood, designed by Helge Vestergaard Jensen for Peder Pedersen.

products.name: Bar cart 'Corall' model AEH SL 23
products.description: Swedish bar cart model AEH SL 23 in elm and black lacquered wood, opening to reveal red-painted bottle shelves and serving trays, mounted on castors with steel handles.

products.name: Bookshelf model 879 by Typenko
products.description: Sculptural bookshelf model 879 in ebonised birch, its asymmetric stepped silhouette giving the piece a strongly contemporary character.

products.name: Cabinet ‘Hug’ designed by Rasmus Appel
products.description: Cabinet 'Hug' in pine with a sculptural folding design, its doors opening outward to reveal coloured trays and compartments on a tall splayed frame.

products.name: Cabinet model 208 in Oregon pine
products.description: Cabinet model 208 in warm Oregon pine, fitted with an interior of small drawers and open compartments, raised on square tapered legs.

products.name: Cabinet model 2135 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: The cabinet stands on slender legs, maintaining an airy, lightweight appearance that aligns with Frank’s preference for furniture that feels open rather than heavy or imposing. Josef Frank’s design philosophy, which emphasised both practicality and visual harmony, is evident in the cabinet’s thoughtful proportions and refined material choices.

products.name: Cabinet
products.description: Cabinet with four mahogany drawers fitted with brass swing handles, crowned by a black marble top and brass-capped feet.

products.name: Cabinet designed by Ole Wanscher for Illums Bolighus
products.description: This beautiful rosewood cabinet by Ole Wanscher was retailed through the established interior firm Illums Bolighus set in Copenhagen during the mid-20th century. The cabinet has vertically ribbed tambour doors that slide to either side, concealing the storage compartment behind.

products.name: Cabinet 'Wellpappskapet' model 2192
products.description: Cabinet 'Wellpappskapet' model 2192 with a corrugated green-lacquered front, walnut frame and brass details, opening to reveal walnut-lined shelving.

products.name: Chest of drawers for DUX
products.description: A chest of drawers produced by DUX during the 1960s, constructed from bamboo and woven rattan. The front is arranged with two smaller drawers above two wider drawers, framed by rounded bamboo elements and wrapped corner details.

products.name: Chest of drawers model OW 9042 in mahogany
products.description: Chest of drawers model OW 9042 in flame-grained mahogany with brass swing handles and a gently bowed front, raised on tall tapered legs.

products.name: Chest of drawers model OW 9043 in mahogany
products.description: Tall chest of drawers model OW 9043 in mahogany with eight drawers, brass swing handles and a curved front on splayed feet.

products.name: Chest of drawers 'Model RY 250' designed by Hans J. Wegner for Ry Møbler
products.description: The 'Model RY 250' chest of drawers designed by Hans J. Wegner and produced by Ry Møbler in Denmark in 1965 is veneered in rosewood, with four drawers, integrated metal handles and round legs in dark-stained solid oak. The model reflects Wegner’s precise understanding of proportion, craftsmanship and functional detail.

products.name: Chest of drawers from the 'Triva' series designed for Nordiska Kompaniet
products.description: 'Trivia' series chest of drawers designed for Nordiska Kompaniet and produced in the company’s own workshop in Nyköping, Sweden. Executed in teak veneer with contrasting black lacquered metal frame and legs, it features three drawers fitted with distinctive circular brass pulls, with the original key retained.

products.name: Dresser and Mirror set designed by Aksel Kjersgaard, Denmark
products.description: Dresser and mirror set in rosewood with three sculpted drawers and a tall rectangular mirror, designed by Aksel Kjersgaard.

products.name: Hall table
products.description: Hall table in yellow lacquer with a stepped asymmetric body combining a cabinet, a drawer and open storage on slender legs, finished with turned black knobs.

products.name: Pair of wall shelves
products.description: This pair of wall-mounted shelves was produced in Sweden during the 1950s. Each unit features a rectilinear open cube flanked by a horizontal shelf, creating a composition that is both geometric and functional.

products.name: Room divider
products.description: Originally a fixture in Magasin du Nord in Aarhus, Denmark. Magasin du Nord in Aarhus is a department store located in the heart of the city, offering a curated selection of fashion, beauty, homeware, and lifestyle products.

products.name: Rosewood bar table by Leif Alring
products.description: Compact bar table in rosewood by Leif Alring, its fold-down front revealing a red felt-lined interior with serving trays and bottle shelving.

products.name: Rosewood dresser designed by Henning Korch for CFC Silkeborg
products.description: This dresser was designed by Henning Korch for the cabinetmaker C.F. Christensen in Silkeborg. It is constructed in rosewood with expressive palisander veneer creating a continuous surface so the natural grain becomes a defining element of the piece.

products.name: Secretary cabinet model 2113 in mahogany and walnut
products.description: Secretary cabinet model 2113 in mahogany and walnut, with a fall-front writing surface, fitted pigeonholes and a bank of small drawers beside open shelving.

products.name: Serving trolley model 2777 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Josef Frank’s model 2777 serving trolley, designed in the 1950s, was crafted from mahogany and features a sleek black Arborite top with the same material used on both shelves below the surface. It has brass handles that add an elegant contrast and enhance its sophistication.

products.name: Serving trolley model 889 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn, Sweden
products.description: The trolley, model 889, by Josef Frank is a prime example of design from the Swedish Grace movement. The design of the trolley references neoclassicism, drawing inspiration from objects found in Ancient Greece and Rome.

products.name: Set of eight shelves
products.description: Stackable.

products.name: Sewing box designed by Magnus L. Stephensen for Axel Søllner
products.description: Magnus Læssøe Stephensen was a renowned mid-century Danish architect whose revolutionary approach to design did away with the extravagant flourishes of the time. Inspired by the simplicity of Bauhaus and Japanese arts and crafts, Stephensen's designs focused on clean lines and practicality.

products.name: Shelf designed by Alvar Andersson for Hyresgästernas Möbelaffär
products.description: Shelf in black lacquered wood with metal inlays along its edges, formed as a tall open bookcase on a recessed plinth.

products.name: Shelf 'Book crib' model T-709 designed by Bruno Mathsson for Firma Karl Mathsson
products.description: Bruno Mathsson’s “Book crib” model T-709 is a refined example of Scandinavian vintage design where function and sculpture are perfectly aligned. Originally conceived in 1941, this piece was produced by Firma Karl Mathsson in 1964 and reflects the designer’s lifelong interest in reading, comfort and order.

products.name: Shelving unit 'K5 wall shelf Type 1' designed by Claesson Koivisto Rune for ADX
products.description: Shelving unit from the K5 series in steel, a modular wall-hung square frame with shelving at two levels.

products.name: Sideboard model 1148 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: This sideboard, model 1148, was designed by Josef Frank in the 1950s for Svenskt Tenn and reflects the designer’s characteristic balance between elegance and practicality. Executed in walnut with surfaces in richly patterned alder root veneer, the piece combines restrained structural lines with gently curved details.

products.name: Sideboard model 2106 in pyramid mahogany
products.description: Sideboard model 2106 in pyramid mahogany with birch edging, four serpentine doors and brass fittings, raised on tapering legs.

products.name: Sideboard designed by Erik Wørts for Kjellerup Møbelfabrik
products.description: This Danish sideboard by Erik Wørts for Kjellerup Møbelfabrik is a refined example of mid-century Scandinavian furniture, where practical storage is combined with disciplined proportions and carefully considered material contrast. The cabinet body is crafted in oak and the base and tapered legs are executed in wenge, introducing a darker visual anchor that emphasises the lightness of the upper form.

products.name: Sideboard model JF 8124 in walnut with brass hardware
products.description: Long sideboard model JF 8124 with a white lacquered body, walnut top and brass hardware, its interior fitted with drawers, cabinets and open shelving.

products.name: Sideboard model JF 8381 in walnut and brass
products.description: Sideboard model JF 8381 in walnut with brass swing handles, arranged with a central bank of small drawers between cabinet doors on slender legs.

products.name: Sideboard for Lysberg, Hansen & Therp
products.description: Sideboard in rosewood with brass details, its three central drawers flanked by cabinet doors and raised on slender tapering legs.

products.name: Storage box/container on wheels
products.description: Small rollable teak box Cubic shape with mitered edges and distinctive prong connections.

products.name: Unique cabinet model OS 8953 in burr ash
products.material: Burr Ash Veneer & Stained Birch & Brass
products.description: Unique cabinet model OS 8953 in burr ash veneer on a stained birch stand, its doors incised with Nordic figurative motifs and finished with brass details.

products.name: Bar cabinet designed by Sture Lindholm for Per Jönssons Verkstäder
products.description: The cabinet is made of teak with darker-stained tapered legs. The front features two hinged doors with a central lock.

products.name: Wall cabinet
products.description: Wall cabinet in pine with a gently bowed door and a single shelf inside, fitted with a simple turned wooden knob.

products.name: Wall cupboard designed by Lars Larsson and Stig Lönngren for HI-Gruppen
products.description: Wall cupboard in lacquered birch plywood. Closed, the piece presents as a compact, pared-back volume.

products.name: Wall hung cabinet for A. Lagerberg
products.description: An expressive allmoge inspired cabinet that reflects the late 19th century Swedish interest in vernacular craft, a direction championed by designers and workshops such as A. Lagerberg. The piece belongs to the same cultural moment in which Stockholm’s exhibitions of the 1890s highlighted a growing curiosity for new European ideas, alongside a reassessment of national traditions.

products.name: Wall mounted cocktail cabinet designed by Svend Langkilde for Langkilde Møbler
products.description: This wall-mounted cocktail cabinet was designed by Svend Langkilde and produced by Langkilde Møbler in Denmark during the 1950s. Constructed in rosewood, the cabinet is defined by the expressive grain of the veneer, arranged across the doors to create a balanced and visually rich surface.

products.name: Shelving system designed by Bruno Mathsson for Mathsson International
products.description: This wall-mounted shelving system, designed by Bruno Mathsson and produced by Mathsson International in the 1960s, embodies the principles of Scandinavian design with its elegant simplicity and functional versatility. Crafted from beech, the design features slender shelves that rest on gently curved wooden brackets, which extend from vertical wall-mounted rails.

products.name: Childrens bed in the style of Peder Moos made by cabinetmaker Ove Sørensen
products.description: Children's bed in solid teak with caned spindle railings and organically curved head- and footboards, made by cabinetmaker Ove Sørensen in the style of Peder Moos.

products.name: Clothes rack
products.description: Clothes rack model 3419 with a black lacquered metal column on a round stepped base, crowned with playful scrolling chrome wire hooks.

products.name: Folding 'Screen 100' designed by Alvar Aalto for Artek
products.description: The folding Screen 100, designed by Alvar Aalto for Artek in 1936, exemplifies Aalto's innovative approach to form and function. Made from birch, the screen features a series of vertically slatted wooden panels joined together in a flexible, undulating design.

products.name: Magazine rack
products.description: Four-tier magazine rack model 3285 in stained wood with turned spindle shelves on a sculpted sled base.

products.name: Wall hung makeup table with wall lamps and stool by Uno & Östen Kristiansson for Luxus
products.description: Wall-hung makeup table by Uno & Östen Kristiansson for Luxus with a large mirrored panel, two acrylic wall lamps, dovetailed oak drawers and a matching stool.

products.name: Ceiling lamp
products.description: This ceiling lamp is a refined example of Swedish Grace from the 1930s, characterised by its restrained form enriched with decorative detail. The fixture is composed of a circular disc of green-toned glass, often referred to as råglas , etched with stylised stork motifs arranged in a rhythmic, symmetrical composition.

products.name: Artichoke pendant
products.description: Sculptural artichoke pendant with concentric tiers of patinated copper leaves around a steel core, in the manner of Poul Henningsen.

products.name: Ceiling lamp model A335B designed by Alvar Aalto for Valaistustyö
products.description: Designed by Alvar Aalto for the Finnish manufacturer Valaistustyö, the 'A335B' ceiling lamp is a distinctive example of his later lighting work. Formed in pressed metal, the lamp is defined by its domed silhouette and the characteristic perforated lower section, which allows light to escape downward in a controlled and rhythmic pattern while maintaining a soft overall glow.

products.name: Six-arm brass chandelier
products.description: Six-arm chandelier in patinated brass with layered opal glass shades on gently curved arms, suspended from a reeded brass column.

products.name: Ceiling lamp designed by Alvar Aalto for Idman
products.description: This ceiling lamp, designed by Alvar Aalto for the Finnish lighting manufacturer Idman in the 1950s, was originally developed for the Stora Enso head office in Helsinki, a landmark building completed in 1962 and designed by Aalto as a total work of art, from façade to interior details. It is a restrained yet highly considered example of his approach to architectural lighting.

products.name: Ceiling lamp model 6022 designed by Gunnar Asplund
products.description: The model was originally created for Gunnar Asplund's music room at the Workshop's exhibition held at Liljevalchs Konsthall in autumn 1920. It became part of Böhlmark's collection in 1922 and remained so until Ateljé Lyktan took over production in 1965.

products.name: Long ceiling lamps designed by Hans Agne Jakobsson
products.description: Designed by Hans Agne Jakobsson, these long ceiling lamps are a distilled expression of Scandinavian lighting from the mid-20th century. Executed in brass and glass, the lamps reflect Jakobsson's broader material experimentation and his belief that lighting should enhance atmosphere rather than dominate it.

products.name: Ceiling lamp designed by Hans-Agne Jakobsson
products.description: Active between the 1950s and 1970s—in the golden age of Scandinavian design—Swedish interior decorator and furniture designer Hans-Agne Jakobsson is best remembered for his softly glowing, glare-free lighting fixtures, which were inspired by the organic modern approaches of Danish lighting master Poul Henningsen and Finnish icon Alvar Aalto. Experimenting with a wide range of materials—including brass, iron, glass, fabric, and wood shavings—Jakobsson mastered both the direction and colour of light.

products.name: Ceiling lamp designed by Helger Johansson for Westal
products.description: Designed in the 1960s by Holger Johansson for Westal, this ceiling lamp is a refined example of Swedish mid-century lighting that balances structure, material and atmosphere. The composition centres on a geometric brass framework from which multiple smoked glass shades are evenly suspended, creating a calm, architectural rhythm while softening the light through the tinted glass.

products.name: Honeycomb ceiling lamp
products.description: Monumental ceiling fixture with a stepped hexagonal frame in patinated copper and glowing amber glass honeycomb diffusers, suspended on three slender rods.

products.name: Chandelier model CA-71
products.description: Chandelier with six opal glass tulip shades on slender brass stems arranged around a polished ring-shaped base.

products.name: Ceiling lamp model SL-31B
products.description: Brass pendant with a smooth dome shade above a pierced snowflake-form diffuser that scatters delicate patterns of light.

products.name: Ceiling lamp designed by Palle Suenson
products.description: Palle Suenson was one of the leading Danish architects of the twentieth century. His style balanced impressive scale and form, always elevated by scrupulous artistic attention to detail and materials.

products.name: Pendant model 8863
products.description: Three-tier pendant with deep green lacquered shades and warm pale-yellow interiors, hung from a nickel-plated socket.

products.name: Ceiling lamp PH 4/4 designed by Poul Henningsen for Louis Poulsen
products.description: Poul Henningsen developed an extensive body of lighting designs built around his pioneering three-shade principle, first introduced in 1926. This system was conceived to produce controlled, glare-free illumination by directing light precisely where it was needed.

products.name: Pendant model 9077
products.description: Pendant with three softly graded amber shades in the classic layered silhouette, giving a warm, glare-free light.

products.name: Set of three ceiling lamps/chandeliers
products.description: Set of three slender brass chandeliers with tubular candle sleeves and bare-bulb detailing.

products.name: Shade lamp model 9076
products.description: Shade pendant in warm patinated copper with three stacked conical shades above a cylindrical lower diffuser.

products.name: Pair of model 324/2 wall lamps for Markaryd
products.description: This pair of wall lamps, model 324/2, was produced in Sweden during the 1960s for Hans-Agne Jakobsson AB in Markaryd. Executed in polished brass, the lamps are defined by their cylindrical shades mounted on adjustable arms, allowing the light to be directed with precision. The construction conceals the light source within the metal form, producing a warm, downward glow that avoids glare. This pair retains its original manufacturer's sticker, confirming its authenticity.

products.name: Pair of wall lights designed by Bertil Brisholm for GA Berg
products.description: Designed in 1938 by Bertil Brisborg for the Swedish manufacturer GA Berg, this pair of wall lights was created as part of a bespoke commission for the LM Ericsson headquarters at Telefonplan in Stockholm. The lamps combine opaline glass shades with refined brass arms, resulting in a balanced interplay between softness and structure. The gently rounded glass diffuses the light evenly, while the angular brass supports introduce a clear architectural presence characteristic of late 1930s Swedish Modern design.

products.name: Pair of wall lamps model V-75 designed by Eje Ahlgren for Bergboms
products.description: This pair of wall lamps was designed by Eje Ahlgren for Bergboms in the 1960s. Each lamp features a hemispherical shade in polished brass, suspended from a horizontal arm attached to a vertical brass stem. The light source is concealed by a white stepped diffuser, designed to provide an even and glare-free illumination.

products.name: Pair of wall lights for the Gävle Theater
products.description: These wall lamps were specially commissioned for the Gävle Theatre, a central hub for the performing arts on Sweden's east coast. Elegantly crafted brass mounts attach the lamps to the wall, and perforated brass detailing at the base of the glass globes allows heat to escape from the light source. The large spherical glass globes diffuse light beautifully, creating a soft, atmospheric glow, while the frosted central glass cylinder ensures an even illumination.

products.name: Pair of wall lamps model V319 designed by Hans Bergström for Ateljé Lyktan
products.description: Designed in 1947 by Hans Bergström for Ateljé Lyktan, the V319 wall lamps are a refined expression of early Swedish modern lighting. The gently flared, conical brass shades are pared back in form and proportion, reflecting Bergström's conviction that light should be white and shine freely. The brushed brass exterior is paired with a white-lacquered interior, allowing the lamps to cast both directed and softly reflected light.

products.name: Pair of wall lamps 'Model 2389' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: The Model 2389 wall lamp by Josef Frank, designed in the 1950s for Svenskt Tenn, exemplifies the designer's refined approach to functional elegance and modernist form. Crafted entirely from polished brass, the lamp features a gracefully curved arm and a wide flared shade that reflect Frank's enduring sense of harmony and proportion. Frank viewed lighting as a central part of interior architecture, favouring indirect light and diffused materials that create a soft, inviting atmosphere.

products.name: Pair of wall lights 'model 2565' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: This pair of wall lights, model 2565, was designed by Josef Frank in the 1950s and produced in Sweden for Svenskt Tenn. The design is centred around a circular wall-mounted reflector plate in polished brass, from which two gently curved candle-like arms extend. The reflector subtly returns light back into the room, contributing to an even, atmospheric illumination rather than a direct or glaring effect.

products.name: Pair of 'Musling' wall lamps model L306 manufactured by Lyfa
products.description: Each lamp features an elegant, organically shaped opal glass shade that diffuses light softly and evenly, creating a warm and atmospheric glow. The sculptural, minimalist form resembles a smooth shell, reflecting the Danish modernist focus on natural inspiration, clean lines, and functional beauty. The use of opal glass highlights Lyfa's dedication to high-quality craftsmanship and its legacy as a key player in Danish lighting.

products.name: Pair of model PH-2/2 wall lamps designed by Poul Henningsen for Louis Poulsen
products.description: This pair of wall lamps, model PH 2/2, was designed by Poul Henningsen and produced by Louis Poulsen in Denmark during the 1930s. The shade system follows Henningsen's three-shade principle, here executed in opal glass, designed to diffuse light evenly while reducing glare. The proportions of the 2/2 configuration produce a controlled, downward-directed illumination suitable for domestic or architectural settings.

products.name: Pair of wall lamps designed by Poul Henningsen
products.description: This model of wall lamp by Poul Henningsen was first introduced in 1931 with metal slats, before being further developed in 1934 into a version using glass elements. Each lamp is constructed from a series of vertically stacked, amber-coloured glass panels that form a cylindrical casing around a tubular light source. The layered arrangement diffuses the light evenly, softening its intensity, and surviving pairs with their original glass components are uncommon.

products.name: Pair of wall lamps designed by Palle Suenson for Louis Poulsen
products.description: This pair of wall lamps was designed in the 1970s by Danish architect Palle Suenson and produced by Louis Poulsen in Denmark. The lamps were originally installed at the Lions College on Tuborgvej in Hellerup, a building designed by Suenson himself, exemplifying his integrated approach to architecture and lighting. Each lamp is formed from a restrained hemispherical composition, combining an upper shade in brass with a lower dome in opaline acrylic that diffuses the light evenly.

products.name: Pair of wall lamps 'Model 6200' designed by Paavo Tynell
products.description: These Model 6200 wall lamps reflect Paavo Tynell's ability to combine restraint with atmosphere. Executed in brass, the elongated shades are delicately perforated with small star-shaped motifs and narrow linear openings, allowing the light to filter softly through the surface. When illuminated, the lamps cast a warm and scattered glow across the wall, creating the intimate, almost celestial effect that became one of Tynell's most recognisable signatures.

products.name: Wall light
products.description: This wall-mounted light was produced in Sweden during the 1980s and consists of a large rectangular metal panel onto which three square elements of varying sizes are mounted in relief. Each square is finished in a different colour — red, green, and black — and conceals an integrated light source that emits indirect illumination onto the surrounding wall surface. The lighting is directed laterally and upward, producing controlled light reflections and soft halos, and the piece is signed.

products.name: Monumental wall lamps designed by Sten Hummel Gumalieus
products.description: Designed in Sweden during the 1950s by architect Sten Hummel Gumaelius, this large-scale wall lamp is fitted with tall opaline glass elements that soften and distribute the light evenly, creating a subdued, non-glare illumination. The model was originally developed for Norrstrandskyrkan in Karlstad, a church building also designed by Hummel Gumaelius and completed at the end of the decade. The lamp was conceived as an integral part of the interior, reflecting a holistic design approach in which lighting was considered inseparable from the architecture itself.

products.name: Floor lamp
products.description: This floor lamp is an elegant example of Swedish Grace, distinguished by its refined classical references and careful craftsmanship. The carved wooden structure is finished in gilt, rising from a quatrefoil base supported by lion's paw feet and articulated with turned and carved details along the stem. The lamp retains its original two-part silk shade, which softens the light and reinforces the period character of the piece. Standing 245 cm tall, it is reportedly associated with the former Hotel Anglais in Stockholm and the design is often attributed to Helge Werner.

products.name: Floor lamp 'Model 2564' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Floor lamp Model 2564 by Josef Frank was designed for Svenskt Tenn and exemplifies his measured approach to materials, proportion and function. This example is executed in brass with an adjustable stem, the circular base raised on finely turned wooden feet, a distinctive detail that introduces warmth and visual lightness. The plain fabric shade reflects Frank's interest in material contrast and balance, and the lamp is stamped by the manufacturer.

products.name: Floor lamp 'Model 2564' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.material: Brass, Black Lacquered Metal & Turned Wood
products.description: Floor lamp Model 2564 by Josef Frank was designed for Svenskt Tenn and exemplifies his measured approach to materials, proportion and function. Executed in brass with black-lacquered details and raised on finely turned wooden feet, this example retains its original dark green metal shade, contributing to the authenticity of the piece. The adjustable stem allows the height and light distribution to be adapted to different interior settings.

products.name: Floor lamp
products.description: This floor lamp is an expressive example of Scandinavian functionalist lighting, where adjustability, material honesty and restrained form were central to design thinking. The construction combines a brass structure with a leather-wrapped central stem, supporting an adjustable arm and height mechanism that allows the light to be positioned precisely according to use. The height varies between 118 and 186 cm, and the fabric shade spreads a soft, even illumination in keeping with the era's ideal of glare-free light.

products.name: Pair of floor lamps model 9602 designed by Paavo Tynell for Taito Oy
products.description: Floor lamp 9602, often referred to as the Chinese Hat, was designed by Paavo Tynell in 1935 for the iconic Hotel Aulanko. Distinguished by its light, graceful rattan shade and cane-covered brass pole, the lamp combines refined elegance with a natural touch. The soft, diffused glow brings a serene and inviting atmosphere to a space, and this pair is stamped Taito Idman and Taito 9602 on the frames.

products.name: Floor lamp A810 designed by Alvar Aalto for Valaisinpaja
products.description: This popular floor light features two hand-riveted shades, each formed from delicate lacquered metal strips, presenting a striking combination of lines and curves and an interesting interplay of direct and indirect light. The stand is finished in hand-sewn black leather, while the neck has a polished brass collar. Floor Light A810 was created by Alvar Aalto in 1959 for the National Pensions Institute in Helsinki, and this example stands 165 cm tall.

products.name: Floor lamp designed by Alf Svensson for Bergboms
products.description: This floor lamp by Alf Svensson for Bergboms is a refined example of Swedish mid-century lighting, combining warm teak, a softly diffused textile shade and stitched leather bindings. The slender tripod structure highlights the natural beauty of the teak, with its rich grain creating a sense of balance between the architectural frame and the lighter, more delicate character of the shade. The design flawlessly reflects Svensson's interpretation of organic modernism, where natural materials and functional simplicity are brought together through elegant proportions.

products.name: Floor lamp for ASEA Belysning
products.description: This ASEA brass floor lamp exemplifies the restrained elegance of Swedish mid-century lighting. The round brass-clad base conceals an internal iron weight and rests on four discreet low feet, giving the lamp visual lightness while ensuring stability. The straight column supports a slender lateral arm, meeting in adjustable joints that allow the light to be raised, lowered and swung to the side with ease, while the domed pressed-brass shade focuses the light gently downward. Marked in the casting ASEA 741118.

products.name: Floor lamp 'Bridge' designed by Severin Hansen Jr.
products.description: The Bridge floor lamp, designed by Severin Hansen Jr for Haslev Møbelsnedkeri in Denmark during the 1950s, exemplifies the refined craftsmanship and organic minimalism of mid-century Scandinavian design. The gently curved, elongated beech stem mirrors the upward growth of a tree trunk, narrowing gracefully toward its brass-mounted top, above which hangs a hand-folded Le Klint pleated shade. The slender tripod base spreads outward in perfect balance, and the switch is subtly integrated between the legs for convenient foot operation.

products.name: Floor lamp model G-33 'Grasshopper' designed by Greta Magnusson Grossman for Bergboms
products.description: The Grasshopper lamp gets its name from its insect-like posture: a dynamic tripod base with a long, angled tubular stem that leans back slightly, supporting an elongated conical shade. This example pairs the brass structure with a black lacquered metal shade and stands 123 cm tall. Greta Magnusson Grossman was a pioneering designer and architect whose work bridged the clean modernism of Scandinavia with a more relaxed California, where she moved in the 1940s and became one of the few women to gain recognition in architecture and industrial design. Designed for Bergboms in Sweden during the 1950s, the lamp is stamped by the manufacturer.

products.name: Floor lamp 'K10-2' designed by Maria Lindeman
products.description: Designed by Maria Lindeman in the 1950s, the K10-2 floor lamp is a refined example of Finnish mid-century lighting. The composition balances a slender black-lacquered stem with polished brass details, while the two adjustable shades allow the light to be directed as needed. Lindeman was trained in Helsinki and became closely associated with Idman, Finland's leading lighting manufacturer of the time.

products.name: Floor lamp 'Model H801' designed by Viljo Hirvonen for Valaistustyö
products.description: This Model H801 floor lamp was designed by Viljo Hirvonen and produced by Valaistustyö in Finland during the 1970s. The design combines a black leather-wrapped base and vertical shaft with white painted metal shades and polished brass details. The counterweighted arms can be repositioned both vertically and directionally, allowing the lamp to function as both task and ambient lighting. The base is stamped Valaistustyö.

products.name: Floor lamp 'Model 2564' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Floor lamp Model 2564 by Josef Frank was designed for Svenskt Tenn and exemplifies his measured approach to materials, proportion and function. The frame is executed in brass, partially black-lacquered, with an adjustable stem that allows the height and light distribution to be adapted to different settings. The shade is covered in Tulpan fabric, adding a rich floral layer to the understated brass construction, and the lamp is stamped by the manufacturer.

products.name: PH 7 floor lamp designed by Poul Henningsen for Louis Poulsen
products.description: This PH 7 floor lamp was designed by Poul Henningsen in 1933 and produced by Louis Poulsen in Denmark. The lamp combines a slender stem with a circular base, a bakelite socket and a set of hand-blown frosted glass shades mounted on a curved arm that positions the light precisely where needed. The carefully calculated shade proportions direct the majority of the light downward without exposing the bulb, making it ideal for reading while still providing a soft ambient glow. Marked with the patent stamp.

products.name: PH 'Waterpump' designed by Poul Henningsen for Louis Poulsen
products.description: The PH Waterpump floor lamp is one of Poul Henningsen's most distinctive reading lights, recognised for its mechanical, almost industrial profile. The long, adjustable arm is raised and lowered by a levered mechanism, a silhouette that quickly earned the lamp its nickname recalling a traditional hand-operated water pump. At the head sits Henningsen's characteristic layered shade system in copper and glass, developed to eliminate glare and distribute light in controlled reflections. First imagined during the war, the earliest models feature a switch integrated into the rocker arm.

products.name: Floor lamp model THV-376 designed by TH. Valentiner for Poul Dinesen
products.description: Crafted from brass, though on occasion found in nickel-plated variants, this fully adjustable floor lamp is a perfectly balanced and understated design. Model THV-376 was produced by Poul Dinesen in Denmark during the 1960s, its slender stem crowned by a deep green lacquered metal shade. TH Valentiner is an elusive designer, the only trace of them being the stamped initials on the base of each lamp produced by Poul Dinesen.

products.name: Floor lamp model 376 designed by TH. Valentiner for Poul Dinesen
products.description: Floor lamp Model 376 was designed by TH Valentiner for Poul Dinesen in Denmark during the 1960s. The lamp combines refined Scandinavian minimalism with precise craftsmanship, featuring a slender adjustable brass arm and stem supporting a conical shade in lacquered metal. The warm brass surface pairs beautifully with the crisp white shade, creating a timeless interplay between light and form suited to both classic and contemporary interiors.

products.name: Table lamp 'model 2434' designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Table lamp model 2434 was designed by Josef Frank in 1939 and produced by Svenskt Tenn. A circular brass base supports a black-lacquered vertical stem, from the upper section of which a flexible brass gooseneck arm extends to carry a colourful conical shade that allows the light to be directed. Model 2434 fits within Svenskt Tenn’s human-centred approach to modern design as a compact, functional lamp intended for everyday use.

products.name: Table lamp model 2466 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: An understated and timeless design, the model 2466 by Josef Frank is found in both a table lamp and a floor lamp silhouette. The brass base structure is encased by lacquered metal, often in a white, black or green tone, with a range of different lampshades available. The simplicity of the design is emblematic of Frank’s lightweight and elegant ideals, reflecting his belief that the home should be personal and comfortable.

products.name: Model 2466 table lamp designed by Josef Frank, Svenskt Tenn
products.description: A refined and timeless design, Josef Frank’s model 2466 is available as both a table and a floor lamp. Its brass base is encased in lacquered metal and complemented by a silk shade, embodying Frank’s vision of lightweight and elegant design. Frank joined Svenskt Tenn in the 1930s, introducing a vibrant and expressive design language that brought warmth and character to interiors.

products.name: Table lamp model 2468 designed by Josef Frank for Svenskt Tenn
products.description: Table lamp model 2468 was designed by Josef Frank in the 1950s and is characterised by its coloured shades, a feature that led to its long-standing nickname, the traffic light lamp. In Frank’s original drawings the shades were conceived in different colours and arranged vertically to create a clear and balanced distribution of light. The lamp combines a playful use of colour with a carefully proportioned structure, making it distinctive within mid-century Scandinavian lighting.

products.name: Table lamp 'Model 61052' designed by Mauri Almari for Idman
products.description: Table lamp model 61052, designed by Mauri Almari in the 1950s, is a refined example of Finnish mid-century lighting where material and atmosphere are closely intertwined. The slender brass frame rises from three looping feet, while the shade is built from closely spaced vertical slats in rattan that filter the light into a gentle interplay of light and shadow. Almari was a central figure in Finnish lighting design, and his work for Idman balances functionality with the atmospheric quality that became a defining aspect of Scandinavian modern lighting.

products.name: Pair of table lamps
products.description: This pair of Swedish table lamps from the 1940s features slender brass columns rising from splayed tripod bases with turned ball details. Each lamp is crowned by a compact off-white fabric shade that spreads an even, diffused light, allowing the pair to work equally well together on a sideboard or separated across a room. The restrained geometry and honest brass finish are characteristic of Swedish design of the period.

products.name: Table lamp model B-075 designed by Eje Ahlgren for Bergboms
products.description: With its sculptural, rounded shade and playful proportions, the B-075 is an outstanding example of Scandinavian mid-century lighting design. The clean construction features a small rod at the top of the shade that allows the light direction to be easily adjusted, and the model belongs to a series of floor and wall lamps sharing the same distinctive shade form. Eje Ahlgren was one of the principal designers at Bergboms during the 1950s and 1960s, the modernist Swedish manufacturer that famously produced Greta Magnusson Grossman’s original Grasshopper lamp.

products.name: Table lamp model B-275 designed by Hans-Agne Jakobsson for Markaryd
products.description: Designed by Hans-Agne Jakobsson, table lamp B-275 exemplifies his enduring commitment to soft, carefully controlled light and functional clarity. The adjustable spherical shade is mounted on a gently curved brass arm, directing the light with precision while maintaining the glare-free illumination for which Jakobsson is best known. His background as an industrial designer informed a language shaped by Organic Modernism, where comfort and visual ease were placed above technical display.

products.name: Rare 'Helmet' table lamp model 9209 designed by Paavo Tynell
products.description: The Helmet table lamp model 9209 was designed by Paavo Tynell in 1950 and stands among the most distinctive Finnish lights of its era. The sleek perforated brass dome casts a warm glow and subtle light patterns, while the rattan-wrapped stem introduces a tactile contrast to the metallic shade and base. Tynell, often called the Poet of Light, played a pivotal role in shaping modern Scandinavian lighting by combining traditional craftsmanship with modern aesthetics.

products.name: Table lamp designed by Per B. Sundberg for Orrefors
products.description: This lamp from 2004 exemplifies Per B. Sundberg’s idiosyncratic approach to combining image, function and form, created during his time at Orrefors. The cast glass base is engraved with a comic-style scene of a jeep speeding through a rural setting, while a red electrical cord is routed along the contours of the base to become part of the composition. The vertical metal stem and white lampshade balance the playful irreverence of the base with a restrained functional profile.

products.name: PH 'Question mark' table lamp designed by Poul Henningsen for Louis Poulsen
products.description: Introduced in 1931, the PH Question Mark table lamp takes its name from the gently curved brass stem that gives the piece both its character and its function. The lamp is built on Henningsen’s seminal three-shade system, here executed in amber-tinted mouthblown glass that conceals the light source and distributes a warm, glare-free glow. The adjustable lamp head swivels along the curve of the stem, exemplifying Henningsen’s belief that good lighting should be both technically precise and visually calm. This example was produced after 1939 and is stamped patented.

products.name: PH 4/3 table lamp designed by Poul Henningsen for Louis Poulsen
products.description: The PH 4/3 table lamp is part of Poul Henningsen’s systematic development of glare-free electric lighting, manufactured by Louis Poulsen from 1926. It belongs to the PH family based on the three-shade principle, where carefully proportioned shades screen the light source and distribute light downward and laterally without exposing the bulb. The designation 4/3 refers to the diameter of the main upper shade and the proportional relationship of the lower shades within the PH system.

products.name: Sculptural table lamp designed by Paul Kedelv for AB Flygsfors Glasbruk
products.description: Designed by Paul Kedelv for AB Flygsfors Glasbruk in the 1960s, this sculptural table lamp exemplifies the expressive direction of Swedish studio glass during the post-war period. The boldly modelled glass body, rendered in a deep red tone and shaped as an abstracted female torso, is raised on a contrasting dark base stamped by Kedelv. Trained at Orrefors under Simon Gate and Edward Hald, Kedelv developed a highly individual language of fluid forms and vivid colour, frequently using the underfång technique in which layers of coloured glass are encased within clear glass.

products.name: Adjustable table lamp designed by TH. Valentiner for Poul Dinesen
products.description: This adjustable table lamp was designed by TH. Valentiner for the Danish manufacturer Poul Dinesen in the 1960s. A slender satin-chromed stem rises from a round base and carries a compact fabric shade that can be tilted to direct the light precisely where needed. The crisp geometry and exacting finish reflect the precise Danish craftsmanship for which both Valentiner and Poul Dinesen are known.

products.name: Bowl designed by Simon Gate for Orrefors, inventory 7307
products.description: This bowl was designed by Simon Gate for Orrefors in Sweden during the 1920s. Gate joined Orrefors in 1916 and helped establish the Graal technique that made the factory internationally celebrated, with his work defining the elegant Swedish Grace style honoured at the 1925 Paris Exhibition. The bowl reflects the refined craftsmanship and balanced classicism for which Orrefors became known between the wars.

products.name: Vase designed by Vicke Lindstrand for Kosta
products.description: This hand-blown glass vase was designed by Vicke Lindstrand for Kosta in the 1950s and is signed LH 1131 / 62 HD. Its teardrop-shaped body rests on a clear glass foot, with an opaque white inner layer enclosed within the transparent outer glass. Lindstrand’s years at Kosta from 1950 to 1973 combined sculptural form, controlled colour and experimentation, making him one of the central figures of twentieth-century Nordic glass.

products.name: Bowl designed by Simon Gate for Orrefors, inventory 7669
products.description: Designed by Simon Gate for Orrefors in 1930, this wide bowl exemplifies the elegant Swedish Grace idiom of the interwar years. Gate helped establish the Graal technique at Orrefors and brought a painterly sensibility to glass that made the factory internationally famous. With its generous 28 cm diameter and low profile, the bowl is a refined example of Orrefors craftsmanship from this period.

products.name: Vase 'Colora' designed by Vicke Lindstrand for Kosta, inventory 301
products.description: This vase belongs to the Colora series that Vicke Lindstrand created at Kosta, in which colour is encapsulated within clear crystal to create a fluid interplay of light. Lindstrand worked at Kosta from 1950 to 1973, a period regarded as one of the most celebrated eras in Swedish glass history and known as his Kostavicke period. The softly sculptural form and playful graphic lines exemplify the essence of Scandinavian modernism for which the series is known.

products.name: Vase 'Colora' designed by Vicke Lindstrand for Kosta, inventory 2158
products.description: This sculptural Colora vase was handcrafted at Kosta and signed Kosta 41673, its deep blue undertones encapsulated within clear crystal glass to create a fluid, organic interplay of light and colour. Lindstrand’s work at Kosta between 1950 and 1973 marked one of the most celebrated eras in Swedish glass history, known as his Kostavicke period. Alongside experimental colour-layered works such as the Colora series, his engraved vases The Pearl Fisherman and The Shark Killer remain highly sought after at international auctions. The vase stands as a museum-quality example of Swedish art glass.

products.name: Vase designed by Erik Höglund for Boda
products.description: This vase was designed by Erik Höglund for Boda in Sweden during the 1950s and stands 27.5 cm tall. Höglund developed a distinctive language of simple, primordial shapes in heavy rustic glass, with coloured elements and air bubbles captured in the mass, deliberately setting himself apart from the polished perfection of earlier Swedish glass art. His conscious non-perfectionism, stamped symbols and sculptural forms made him one of the most original voices of mid-century Swedish glass, celebrated with the Lunning Prize in 1957.

products.name: Vase 'Fabula and Ariel' designed by Per B. Sundberg for Orrefors
products.description: This sculptural glass vase by Per B. Sundberg is titled Fabula and Ariel and was produced for Orrefors in Sweden in 2004. The irregular, organically shaped body is punctuated by multiple lens-like protrusions that refract and distort the imagery embedded within, with softly focused photographic motifs of dogs suspended in rhythmical repetition beneath the transparent surface. These layered distortions amplify the surreal, psychological tone of the work, challenging traditional distinctions between medium, ornament and message. Each piece is individually crafted and the vase is signed.

products.name: Vase 'Fish Graal' designed by Edward Hald for Orrefors, inventory 7774
products.description: This Fish Graal vase was designed by Edward Hald for Orrefors in 1949, a variation of the Graal technique that Hald developed together with Simon Gate and Knut Bergqvist at the Swedish glassworks. In the Fishgraal process a design is painted onto a coloured layer, acid-etched, then reheated and cased beneath a thick layer of crystal so that the motif appears suspended in depth. Hald completed his artistic training with Henri Matisse in Paris, and his nature-inspired vocabulary of fish and plant forms became a hallmark of Swedish Modern glass. As each piece is individually blown and shaped, no two Fish Graal vases are exactly alike.

products.name: Vase 'Fiskgraal' designed by Edward Hald for Orrefors, inventory 11562
products.description: This Fiskgraal vase was designed by Edward Hald for Orrefors during the 1950s and 1960s and stands 15 cm tall. Created in the demanding Graal technique, its engraved fish and plant motifs are encased within multiple layers of glass so that they appear suspended in depth, with each individually blown piece unique. Drawing on his background in painting and his studies in Paris, Hald brought a distinctly modern, nature-inspired vocabulary to the medium. The vase is signed Orrefors Graal Nr. 210 E7.

products.name: Vase 'Höst' designed by Vicke Lindstrand for Kosta
products.description: Designed by Vicke Lindstrand for Kosta in the 1960s, the Höst vase takes its name from the Swedish word for autumn. Dark branching tree forms are suspended within a thick body of clear glass, punctuated by fragments of red, green, yellow and orange that evoke scattered autumn leaves. The composition was produced using the demanding underfång cased-glass technique, which embeds the coloured elements beneath an outer layer of clear crystal so that the trees appear to float almost three-dimensionally within the vessel. The vase is marked LH 1754.

products.name: Vase designed by Per B. Sundberg for Orrefors, inventory 1765
products.description: This vase was designed by Per B. Sundberg for Orrefors in 2004, exploring abstraction through smooth, bulbous forms rendered in glossy white glass. The shape resists traditional symmetry and evokes organic growth or molten flow, while the vibrant red opening introduces a sharp contrast that draws the eye inward. Its highly reflective surface enhances the sculptural presence, giving the piece a sense of movement despite its stillness.

products.name: Vase designed by Per B. Sundberg for Orrefors, inventory 8136
products.description: Produced during Per B. Sundberg’s collaboration with the Swedish glassworks Orrefors, this cylindrical vase from 2003 reflects his interest in surface as both structure and visual language. Vertical black lines of irregular spacing and thickness wrap around the white glass body in a rhythm that recalls hand-drawn marks or abstracted script, with a decoration that appears to shift when viewed from different angles. Form is deliberately restrained, allowing the surface treatment to drive the visual character of the piece.

products.name: Vase 'Savoy', model 3030, designed by Alvar Aalto for Iittala
products.description: The Savoy vase was designed by Alvar Aalto in 1936 and produced by Iittala, its free undulating outline created by blowing molten glass within a wooden mould. Originally developed for a glass competition organised by Iittala, the design gained its name after being selected for the interior of Helsinki’s Savoy Hotel, designed by Aalto with his wife Aino. Standing 16 cm high and 21 cm long, the vase marked a departure from rigid geometric forms in favour of an organic design rooted in landscape, water and natural movement. Each example carries subtle variations that reflect the hand-crafted nature of its production.

products.name: Vase 'Terra' designed by Monica Backström for Kosta Boda
products.description: This vase from Monica Backström’s Terra series for Kosta Boda, made in 2004, takes its inspiration from the irregular forms and surfaces of the natural world, its softly asymmetric, almost planetary form enveloped in deep midnight-blue glass. The finely mottled surface shifts between blue, grey and metallic tones, while the highly polished exterior contrasts with the mineral-like interior colouring to recall a polished stone or fragment of volcanic rock. Backström was one of the most distinctive figures in modern Swedish glass, drawing on nature, the human body and the cosmos in an experimental approach to texture, colour and sculptural form.
